M20 gains its planned leaves (each with 3 to 5 bounded acceptance lines, touch zones read from the M16 end-state code, and a sheet); the first slice is decided starting from the Claude report's candidates: posture as data, doctor posture gaps, and the harness-settings compiler; the plan covers operation risk labelling (maintainer 2026-11-05): configurable risk levels with defaults (low/medium/high/critical by reversibility and blast radius) whose definitions double as reviewer checklists; deterministic rule-table labels first (zones, paths, diff content, command patterns), an optional model labeller second; labels at planning, at code review (diff riskier than plan is a finding) and in the GUI; labels only escalate scrutiny (extra reviewer, security lens, human confirmation) and never relax a guard or policy

acceptance: A probe (a subcommand of an existing CLI group, plus a runbook step in docs/agentic-sandbox-runbook.md for harnesses it cannot run headless) creates a scratch git repo with a canary instruction carrying a per-run nonce in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, launches each rostered reviewer harness with exactly the command line `review delegate` builds, and reports whether the nonce reached the reviewer's output

Each result is recorded as a harness fact (the M18.2 records) per harness and CLI version: isolated, leaks, or unverified when never captured, with the capture date; harness-facts.schema.json accepts the field
`handoff status` warns when a review record says fresh_session: true and its reviewer ran on a harness and CLI version recorded as leaks; no warning for isolated or unverified

Tests use stub harness commands only (no real CLI, no network): a stub that echoes the nonce is recorded as leaks, one that does not as isolated; the handoff status warning appears for leaks and not otherwise
